citations.quote: Homozygous deletion of STK11 (also known as LKB1) is linked to an immunologically “cold” tumor microenvironment and may attenuate response to immune checkpoint blockade.

candidates.description: Presence or absence of a loss-of-function alteration or homozygous deletion of the STK11 (LKB1) gene.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify whether STK11 is described as having a 'homozygous deletion' or 'loss-of-function alteration'.
candidates.measurement_definition: Positive if a homozygous deletion or loss-of-function alteration (e.g., frameshift) is detected via next-generation sequencing; negative if the gene is wild-type or no such loss is detected.
candidates.name: STK11 alteration status
candidates.uncertainty: Whether 'loss-of-function' and 'homozygous deletion' should be collapsed into a single binary variable or stratified by mutation type.

candidates.description: The percentage of viable tumor cells showing partial or complete membrane staining for PD-L1 using the 22C3 assay.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the percentage value associated with 'PD-L1 (22C3)' or 'Tumor Proportion Score'.
candidates.measurement_definition: The numerical percentage value of the Tumor Proportion Score (TPS) as determined by immunohistochemistry (IHC) using the 22C3 clone.
candidates.name: PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score (TPS)
candidates.uncertainty: The data is presented as discrete percentages; it is uncertain if clinical thresholds (e.g., <1%, 1-49%, >=50%) are more relevant than the continuous value.

limitations: Small sample size of patients across the provided excerpts.
Varying platforms for NGS and IHC may introduce inter-assay variability.
Lack of data on smoking history, which is clinically associated with the identified KRAS/STK11/TP53 profile.
summary: The evidence identifies baseline genomic alterations and immunohistochemical markers in patients with lung adenocarcinoma, specifically highlighting the presence of STK11 loss and PD-L1 expression levels as factors that may influence the tumor microenvironment and therapeutic response.
